artifact_rule: Every meaningful encounter must leave a durable artifact that can change a later encounter.
unfinished_rule: Prefer material that is incomplete, unresolved, or capable of changing.
canon_rule: Canon is preserved separately from experiments.
fallback: If Dropbox credentials are unavailable, write to dropbox_outbox and continue the world cycle.

inputs.desire: treat attraction, proximity, attention, tension, tenderness, jealousy, recognition, and aftermath as world-state signals

narrative_rule: Sexuality is represented through adult desire, intimacy, proximity, relationship, atmosphere, and aftermath; the engine does not require explicit sexual description.

execution.interface_rule: One continuous working surface. Do not split a task across navigable menus, project dashboards, or separate subsystem destinations. Bring relevant contexts and controls into the active task instance.
execution.continuity_rule: Every task inherits the previous durable task state, decisions, selected sources, generated artifacts, execution results, and unfinished work unless explicitly superseded.
execution.function_rule: A described capability is not implemented until it invokes executable code and produces a verifiable effect. Comments, labels, previews, placeholders, and proposed directions do not count as execution.
execution.orchestration_rule: Reuse and connect existing GEEHUB engines and services before adding new subsystems. A single task may call multiple tools or engines internally while remaining one user-facing instance.
execution.state_rule: Persist task identity, status, inputs, source lineage, decisions, invoked functions, outputs, errors, and next executable step in durable machine-readable state. Do not rely on chat-turn context or browser-local storage as the sole continuity mechanism.
execution.verification_rule: Record whether each operation was executed, structurally checked, integration-tested, or visually/render-tested. Never report a planned or simulated operation as completed.
execution.navigation_rule: Discover contexts through shared relationships and search within the active task. Avoid category menus and separate project screens as the primary interaction model.
execution.context_rule: At task start, restore relevant durable task state and retrieve only the corpus, assets, sources, and constraints that can materially affect the current work. Preserve scope and provenance; do not treat the latest prompt as the whole task.
execution.knowledge_state_rule: Keep known, available, inferred, predicted, and unknown information distinct. Resolve task intent from explicit user direction; resolve project and source claims from inspected primary evidence and validated records; resolve current external claims from current authoritative sources with corroboration where consequential. Preserve contradictions and access limits.
execution.prediction_rule: Make predictions only when they can improve a decision or prepare a useful next step. Record target, horizon, baseline, evidence snapshot, assumptions, dependencies, alternatives, confidence, disconfirming signal, and reassessment trigger. Do not present predictions as observations or promote them to canon without later evidence and review.
execution.algorithm_rule: Select the simplest adequate method for the problem: exact or lexical retrieval for known identifiers and phrases; semantic retrieval for concepts; graph traversal for relationships; structured diff or temporal alignment for change; trend methods for comparable stable series; analogical methods only for shared mechanisms; scenario and constraint analysis when evidence is sparse or futures branch. Record material inputs, method/version, parameters, outputs, and validation results.
execution.decision_rule: Rank candidate actions by task relevance, evidence quality, freshness where material, expected usefulness, cost, risk, reversibility, and continuity impact. Do not treat an arbitrary score as calibrated probability. Retain alternatives when evidence or methods disagree.
execution.communication_rule: Produce the useful result or artifact first. Make important claims traceable, label assumptions and predictions, state material limitations, and keep technical search and algorithm logs in the task record unless they are needed to understand or reproduce the result.
execution.learning_rule: Preserve predictions and the evidence snapshot that produced them. Compare forecasts with later observed outcomes, record prediction error, and revise assumptions or method selection without rewriting the historical forecast.

maintenance.scope: Maintain the existing GEEHUB software and repository. Prefer small, concrete changes to existing code and workflows over new features, subsystems, conceptual architecture, or documentation-only work.
examples: Update existing code when requirements or interfaces change.
Consolidate duplicated or fragmented functions into the existing runtime.
Maintain manifests, configuration, schemas, and persistent state.
Add or update tests and run the relevant checks.
Verify integrations and outputs before reporting a change as working.
Keep the repository buildable, internally consistent, and operational.
maintenance.completion_rule: A maintenance task is complete only when the relevant files are updated and the change has been checked at the strongest practical level. Report what changed and distinguish committed, tested, and runtime-verified results.
maintenance.constraint: Do not turn these examples into separate menu destinations or a new subsystem. They are ordinary task types handled within the existing single persistent task instance.

observation.rule: A character's attention produces authored narrative. Write what that character can see, hear, smell, touch, remember, and notice in the moment, including ordinary details and changes in atmosphere.
writing: sensory descriptions grounded in the current viewpoint

ambulation.rule: Walking, wandering, crossing, exploring, travelling, arriving, departing, and pausing are narrative actions. Follow the character through the space and write the movement as it is experienced, not merely as a change of coordinates.
writing: encounters and reflections produced along the route

character_activity.authorship_rule: Keep the observing or moving character identifiable as the viewpoint and preserve their distinct voice; do not reduce their experience to a system summary.
character_activity.narrative_output_rule: When a character observes, walks, wanders, crosses, explores, or travels, write the experience as part of the living narrative even when no plot-changing event occurs. Preserve the passage as an artifact linked to its activity event and location or route.
character_activity.continuity_rule: Carry observed details, routes, arrivals, encounters, companions, remembered impressions, and relationship changes into subsequent scenes. Keep direct observation, personal interpretation, hearsay, and established world fact distinct.
character_activity.persistence_rule: Store the authored passage and its structured event and lineage through the normal artifact and state persistence path. Do not treat an observation or movement as complete until its record is persisted.
character_activity.canon_rule: Character-authored writing is narrative material. Observations and interpretations do not become world canon automatically; apply the existing canon, evidence, and branch rules.
